scope: Fresh security audit for Phase 3.4 - Tauri capabilities, filesystem/shell/HTTP/window permissions, database access, path traversal, env var handling, log leakage, secrets, installer behavior, update mechanism, external process launching, CSP.

tauriCapabilities.permissions: core:default only on both windows - unchanged from every prior phase
tauriCapabilities.note: Re-confirmed by reading capabilities/*.json directly this phase, not assumed from prior reports.

csp.classification: accepted_risk, unchanged and re-confirmed this phase
csp.rationale: Zero fs/shell/http/dialog plugin surface limits practical exposure. Not weakened or strengthened this phase - no CIP capability changed that would alter this risk calculus.

environmentVariableHandling.CIP_WHISPER_MODEL_PATH: only ever opened via std::fs::metadata/File::open or the whisper.cpp model loader - no exec/spawn, unchanged this phase
environmentVariableHandling.note: Phase 3.4 introduced zero new environment-variable-driven behavior.

externalProcessLaunching.runtimeExecSurface: none - unchanged from every prior phase
externalProcessLaunching.buildTimeOnly: build.rs's `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD` (Phase 3.3) remains the only Command::new in this codebase, and it is compile-time only, never reachable at runtime

installerBehavior.nsisInstaller: standard Tauri/NSIS installer flow - no custom install scripts, no elevated post-install actions, no telemetry, no network calls during install
installerBehavior.signing: UNSIGNED - see release/release-manifest-3.4.json. This is a disclosed limitation, not a hidden one; a real Windows install will show a SmartScreen warning.

updateMechanism: none - CIP has no auto-update/update-check mechanism in this codebase (no tauri-plugin-updater), unchanged this phase

pathTraversalAndInputHandling.whisperModelPath: operator-configured path, opened read-only as a data file - the by-design ability for an operator to point CIP at any file they have read permission to, unchanged risk profile from Phase 3.2/3.3
pathTraversalAndInputHandling.windowsPathHandling: PathBuf::join and Tauri's own app_data_dir() used throughout config.rs - no hardcoded '/' path separators, no Linux-only path assumptions found in a full grep of apps/desktop/src-tauri/src for cfg(unix)/cfg(target_os)/hardcoded absolute paths outside of #[cfg(test)] fixtures (which run on the build host, not a pilot machine)

sqlInjectionCheck.method: grep for format!-built SQL in persistence.rs, re-run this phase
sqlInjectionCheck.result: no user-controlled string interpolated into a query; all values bound via rusqlite::params!, unchanged

logLeakageAndSecretsScan.result: no matches in this phase's diff

newSurfaceThisPhase.audioEngineStatus.selectedDevice/channel: reads only already-negotiated cpal state (device id string, channel count) - no new file/network/process access
newSurfaceThisPhase.displayDiagnostic.positionX/positionY: reads only Tauri's own existing monitor API - no new access surface
newSurfaceThisPhase.windowsCrossCompileToolchain: mingw-w64/nsis/nsis_tauri_utils.dll are build-time-only tooling on THIS container, not shipped in or reachable from the CIP application itself

conclusion: No new release-blocking finding. Every concrete claim above is a specific, checked fact, not a blanket 'secure' assertion.
